correctionRecord.what: The named blocker -- 'KL-000 independent reimplementation' -- was discharged by evidence this record predates, and the record did not know it. The blocker text below is preserved verbatim as superseded, not rewritten.
correctionRecord.evidence: IND-20260807-1/-2/-3 (KL-000/results/independent/): a zero-dependency Rust implementation with hand-written JSON, SHA-256 and PRNG, written from the registered documents, agreeing with the reference on the evaluator's exhaustive partitioning, the complete conclusion function (160/49,480/41,820/19,380 over all 110,840 receipts), and the canonical form and digests for the two pinned receipts C11/C12 (byte-identical, 703 and 691 bytes). Commissioned ONCE, exactly as the superseded text said it should be, serving both KL-000's gate and this kernel's prerequisite. Qualified by LEAK-101 as recorded in KL-000/FINAL-RECORD.md; the qualification travels with any KL-011 use of this artifact too.
correctionRecord.pattern: This is the stale-self-description family again -- a record whose truth expired while the world moved, detected by re-deriving from evidence rather than reading the record. Prior instances: PROV-005 (a deleted remote's cache measured as the remote), ART-101 (a result artifact carrying its predecessor's identity), TEST-101 (a projected verification value inherited unexecuted for three runs), and the DOC-102 miscount chain. The fix is the same every time: records name their evidence, and reviews re-derive rather than re-read. This record now cites what discharged its blocker instead of asserting the blocker.

nextGate: A transport that is not of our own construction. This run crossed a process boundary through bytes we serialised with a codec we chose. A2.question: does presence require complete coverage?
A2.decision: NO -- a found counterexample stands regardless of coverage
A2.note: This is what the v0.1 evaluator already does; the decision removes an ambiguity that let two conforming implementations diverge on 17.3% of receipts, and changes no behaviour. Registered and pinned by tests in tests/test_transaction_v2.py. The asymmetry with absence is deliberate: absence is a claim about everything not found, presence is a claim about something that was.

SCH-005.question: protected fields the receipt never emitted
SCH-005.decision: ADD them to the receipt, in a v0.2 evaluator
SCH-005.note: RESEARCH-DIRECTION.md always specified unattributed evidence, uncertainty, declared shared dependencies and the reason for abstention. v0.1 emitted none. The omission has a shape: everything emitted expresses confidence, everything absent expresses doubt. Narrowing the claim to match the code was considered and rejected -- it would have deleted the requirement rather than met it. v0.1 is pinned by SHA-256 in four KL-000 registrations and is untouched; the fields live in knowledge_ledger/transaction_v2.py at schema v0.2.

v02Outcome.ablations: Each endpoint was shown able to fail. A lossy transport was substituted for the faithful one, once per endpoint, and each ablation turned exactly its own endpoint red and no other: uncertainty stripped -> E3 only (30), roots stripped -> E1 only (30), coverage forced complete -> E2 only (34), conclusion overwritten -> E4 only (46), authority field injected -> E5 only (64). A clean diagonal, so the endpoints discriminate and do not overlap. Without this the 350/350 pass would be indistinguishable from a comparison that cannot fail.
v02Outcome.crossingIsReal: Invalidation clause I1 requires the arms share no in-memory object. The crossed arm spawns a separate interpreter and reaches it only through serialised bytes on a pipe.

recordHygieneFinding.novelty: First instance ACROSS repositories rather than within one. Prior instances (PROV-005, ART-101, TEST-101, DOC-102, and this experiment's own blocker corrected at RUN-20260807-6) were each caught by a review that re-derived rather than re-read. No such review spans repositories, so this one was caught by the owner's memory instead.
